sentences.zh: 王伯大 鄭寀 應㒡 徐清叟 李曾伯 王野 蔡抗 張磻 馬天驥 朱熠 饒虎臣 戴慶炣 皮龍榮 沈炎

translations.literal: Wang Boda, Zheng Cai, Ying You, Xu Qingsou, Li Cengbo, Wang Ye, Cai Kang, Zhang Pan, Ma Tianji, Zhu Yi, Rao Huchen, Dai Qingke, Pi Longrong, Shen Yan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Boda, Zheng Cai, Ying You, Xu Qingsou, Li Cengbo, Wang Ye, Cai Kang, Zhang Pan, Ma Tianji, Zhu Yi, Rao Huchen, Dai Qingke, Pi Longrong, and Shen Yan

sentences.zh: 王伯大

translations.literal: Wang Boda
translations.idiomatic: Wang Boda

sentences.zh: 王伯大，字幼學，福州人。

translations.literal: Wang Boda, courtesy name Youxue, was a man of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Boda, styled Youxue, was a native of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the seventh year of Jiading (1214).

sentences.zh: 歷官主管戶部架閣，遷國子正、知臨江軍，歲饑，振荒有法。

translations.literal: He served in office as supervisor of the Ministry of Revenue archives, was promoted to Rectifier of the Directorate of Education and made prefect of Linjiang Circuit; in a year of famine he had effective methods for famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as supervisor of the Ministry of Revenue archives, he was promoted to Rectifier of the Directorate of Education and appointed prefect of Linjiang; when famine struck that year, his famine relief measures were notably effective.

sentences.zh: 遷國子監丞、知信陽軍，改知池州兼權江東提舉常平。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and made prefect of Xinyang Circuit, then transferred to be prefect of Chizhou while concurrently acting as Jiangdong intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and prefect of Xinyang, and later transferred to Chizhou as acting Jiangdong intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 久之，依舊直秘閣、江東提舉常平，仍兼知池州。

translations.literal: After some time he was restored to his former posts as direct academician of the Secret Archive and Jiangdong intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries, while still concurrently serving as prefect of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was reappointed direct academician of the Secret Archive and Jiangdong intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries, while continuing as prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 端平三年，召至闕下，遷尚右郎官，尋兼權左司郎官，遷右司郎官、試將作監兼右司郎中，兼提領鎮江、建寧府轉般倉，兼提領平江府百萬倉，兼提領措置官田。

translations.literal: In the third year of Duanping he was summoned to the capital, promoted to Senior Right Bureau Gentleman, and soon given concurrent duty as acting Left Bureau Gentleman; he was then made Right Bureau Gentleman and acting Director of Palace Construction while also Right Bureau Senior Gentleman, and concurrently supervised the transit granaries of Zhenjiang and Jianning prefectures, the Million-Grain Granary of Pingjiang, and the arrangement of official fields.
translations.idiomatic: In 1236 (Duanping 3) he was called to court, made Senior Right Bureau Gentleman, and soon given acting duty in the Left Bureau; he then became Right Bureau Gentleman and acting Director of Palace Construction with concurrent charge of the Zhenjiang and Jianning transit granaries, the Pingjiang million-grain storehouse, and the management of official farmland.

sentences.zh: 進直寶謨閣、樞密副都承旨兼左司郎中。

translations.literal: He was advanced to direct academician of the Baomo Pavilion and Deputy Chief Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs while also serving as Left Bureau Senior Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct academician of the Baomo Pavilion and Deputy Chief Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, retaining his post as Left Bureau Senior Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 進對，言：

translations.literal: Presenting himself at audience, he said:
translations.idiomatic: At an audience with the emperor he said:

sentences.zh: 今天下大勢如江河之決，日趨日下而不可挽。

translations.literal: Now the great trend of the realm is like a river bursting its banks, daily rushing downward and beyond recall.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's situation today is like a river in flood, rushing ever downward with no way to turn it back.

sentences.zh: 其始也，搢紳之論，莫不交口誦詠，謂太平之期可矯足而待也；

translations.literal: At first, among the gentry none failed to speak with one voice in praise, saying that an age of great peace could be awaited with a mere lifting of the heel;
translations.idiomatic: At first the talk among officials was unanimous in celebration, holding that an age of peace was only a step away;

sentences.zh: 未幾，則以治亂安危之制為言矣；

translations.literal: before long they spoke instead of the measures governing order and disorder, safety and danger;
translations.idiomatic: before long they were speaking of measures for order, disorder, safety, and peril;

sentences.zh: 又未幾，則置治安不言而直以危亂言矣；

translations.literal: again before long they set aside talk of peace and order and spoke directly of peril and turmoil;
translations.idiomatic: soon after they ceased to speak of peace and security and spoke outright of crisis and chaos;

sentences.zh: 又未幾，則置危亂不言而直以亡言矣。

translations.literal: and again before long they set aside peril and turmoil and spoke directly of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: and still later they set crisis aside and spoke only of extinction.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，以亡為言，猶知有亡矣，今也置亡而不言矣。

translations.literal: Alas! To speak of ruin at least shows that ruin is still known; now ruin is set aside and no longer spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—even to speak of ruin still meant ruin was acknowledged; now even ruin goes unmentioned.

sentences.zh: 人主之患，莫大乎處危亡而不知；

translations.literal: For a ruler there is no greater calamity than to be in peril and ruin without knowing it;
translations.idiomatic: For a sovereign there is no greater peril than to stand in danger of ruin without knowing it;

sentences.zh: 人臣之罪，莫大乎知危亡而不言。

translations.literal: for a minister there is no greater fault than to know of peril and ruin yet not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: and for a minister there is no greater fault than to know the realm is in peril yet remain silent.

sentences.zh: 陛下親政，五年於茲，盛德大業未能著見於天下，而招天下之謗議者何其籍籍而未已也？

translations.literal: Your Majesty has personally governed for five years now, yet your great virtue and great undertakings have not been clearly seen throughout the realm, while the slanders and criticisms that draw the realm's talk—how numerous and unceasing they are!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has held personal rule for five years, yet your great virtue and achievements have not made themselves felt throughout the land, while criticism and rumor about the court—how thick and unending they remain!

sentences.zh: 議逸欲之害德，則天下將以陛下為商紂、周幽之人主；

translations.literal: When they discuss how indulgence harms virtue, the realm will take Your Majesty for a ruler like King Zhou of Shang or King You of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: When critics speak of how licentious desire undermines virtue, the realm will compare Your Majesty to King Zhou of Shang or King You of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 議戚宦近習之撓政，則天下將以朝廷為恭、顯、許、史、武、韋、仇、魚之朝廷；

translations.literal: when they discuss how kinsmen, eunuchs, and close favorites obstruct government, the realm will take this court for the courts of Gong, Xian, Xu, Shi, Wu, Wei, Qiu, and Yu;
translations.idiomatic: when they speak of how imperial kin, eunuchs, and intimate favorites warp policy, the realm will see this court as no better than those of Gong, Xian, Xu, Shi, Wu, Wei, Qiu, and Yu;

sentences.zh: 議奸儔佞朋之誤國，則天下又將為漢黨錮、元祐黨籍之君子。

translations.literal: when they discuss how wicked companions and flatterers in factions mislead the state, the realm will again take your worthy men for the gentlemen of the Han faction proscription and the Yuanyou party register.
translations.idiomatic: when they speak of how treacherous cliques and sycophantic factions mislead the state, the realm will again treat your upright men as victims of the Han faction ban or the Yuanyou party lists.

sentences.zh: 數者皆犯前古危亡之轍跡，忠臣懇惻而言之，志士憤激而和之。

translations.literal: Each of these touches the tracks of peril and ruin in former ages; loyal ministers speak with earnest sincerity, and men of resolve echo them in indignant passion.
translations.idiomatic: Each charge retraces the path to ruin in ages past; loyal ministers speak with anguished sincerity, and men of principle answer them in righteous anger.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖日御治朝，日親儒者，日修辭飾色，而終莫能弭天下之議。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty daily presides over the governing court, daily draws near Confucian scholars, and daily polishes words and appearance, in the end you cannot still the realm's criticisms.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty daily holds court, daily keeps company with scholars, and daily polishes speech and demeanor, you still cannot quiet the talk of the realm.

sentences.zh: 言者執之而不肯置，聽者厭之而不憚煩，於是厭轉而為疑，疑增而為忿，忿極而為愎，則罪言黜諫之意藏伏於陛下之胸中，而凡迕己者皆可逐之人矣。

translations.literal: The speakers hold to their words and will not let go; the listener grows weary and is not afraid of the trouble—then weariness turns to suspicion, suspicion grows to anger, and anger at its height becomes obstinacy; then the intent to blame speech and dismiss remonstrance lies hidden in Your Majesty's breast, and all who cross you may be driven away.
translations.idiomatic: Speakers cling to their charges and will not relent; the listener grows weary and ceases to heed them—weariness turns to suspicion, suspicion to anger, and anger at last to obstinacy; then the wish to punish speech and silence remonstrance lodges in Your Majesty's heart, and anyone who crosses you becomes fit for dismissal.

sentences.zh: 彼中人之性，利害不出於一身，莫不破厓絕角以阿陛下之所好。

translations.literal: Those of middling character, whose profit and loss do not extend beyond their own persons, all break their horns and cut their corners to flatter what Your Majesty favors.
translations.idiomatic: Men of middling character, whose interests begin and end with themselves, all trim their principles to curry favor with Your Majesty's tastes.

sentences.zh: 其稍畏名義者，則包羞閔默而有跋前疐後之憂；

translations.literal: those who somewhat fear reputation and right principle wrap themselves in shame and keep silent, with the worry of advancing and then stumbling;
translations.idiomatic: Those who still care for reputation swallow their shame and hold their tongues, fearful of advancing only to be checked;

sentences.zh: 若其無所顧戀者，則皆攘袂遠引，不願立於王之朝矣。

translations.literal: while those who have nothing left to hold them back all roll up their sleeves and withdraw far away, unwilling to stand in the king's court.
translations.idiomatic: while those with nothing left to lose all throw up their sleeves and withdraw, unwilling to remain at the royal court.

sentences.zh: 陛下試反於身而自省曰：吾之制行，得無有屋漏在上、知之在下者乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty should try turning back upon yourself and reflecting: In my conduct and deportment, might there be what is hidden in the rafters above yet known below?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should turn inward and ask: In my conduct, is there anything hidden in the rafters that those below already know?

sentences.zh: 徒見嬖昵之多，選擇未已，排當之聲，時有流聞，則謂精神之內守，血氣之順軌，未可也。

translations.literal: Yet one only sees many favorites and intimates, selection unceasing, and the sound of backstage arrangements often circulating in rumor—then to say that the spirit is inwardly guarded and the vital forces run in their proper course cannot yet be affirmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one sees only a crowd of favorites, endless selection, and constant rumor of backstage deals—so to claim that your spirit is disciplined and your passions in order cannot yet be believed.

sentences.zh: 陛下又試於宮閫之內而加省曰：凡吾之左右近屬，得無有因微而入，緣形而出，意所狎信不復猜覺者乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty should also try within the inner palace and reflect further: Among all those close at my side, might there be none who enter through slight openings, emerge along hidden paths, and through long familiarity are trusted without further suspicion?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should also look within the palace and ask: Among those at my side, is there no one who slipped in through small openings, acts through hidden channels, and through long familiarity is trusted without further vigilance?

sentences.zh: 徒見內降幹請，數至有司，裏言除臣，每實人口，則謂浸潤之不行，邪徑之已塞，未可也。

translations.literal: Yet one only sees inner palace requests repeatedly reaching the offices, private words removing officials that each time prove true in the mouths of men—then to say that gradual undermining does not occur and crooked paths are already blocked cannot yet be affirmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one sees only palace petitions repeatedly reaching the ministries, private word removing officials that rumor always confirms—so to claim that gradual corruption has ceased and back channels are closed cannot yet be believed.

sentences.zh: 陛下又試於朝廷政事之間而三省曰：凡吾之諸臣，得無有讒說殄行，震驚朕師，惡直醜正，側言改度者乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty should also try amid the court's affairs of state and thrice reflect: Among all my ministers, might there be none who with slander destroy conduct, shock the teacher, hate the upright and abhor the correct, and with sidelong words alter the law?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should also examine the court and thrice ask: Among my ministers, is there no one who slanders the upright, shocks his teacher, hates integrity, and with crooked speech bends policy?

sentences.zh: 徒見剛方峭直之士，昔者所進，今不知其亡，柔佞闒茸之徒，適從何來，而遽集於斯也，則謂舉國皆忠臣，聖朝無闕事，未可也。

translations.literal: Yet one only sees that firm and upright men once advanced are now gone without trace, while the soft, flattering, and base—whence did they just come that they suddenly gather here?—then to say that the whole state is loyal ministers and the sage court has no shortcoming cannot yet be affirmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one sees only that the firm and upright whom you once advanced have vanished, while the soft, flattering, and base—whence did they come, that they now crowd the court?—so to claim that every subject is loyal and the sage reign lacks fault cannot yet be believed.

sentences.zh: 夫以陛下之好惡用舍，無非有招致人言之道；

translations.literal: As for Your Majesty's likes and dislikes, employment and dismissal—there is nothing that does not contain a way of drawing men's talk;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's likes and dislikes, appointments and dismissals—all invite public talk;

sentences.zh: 及人言之來，又復推而不受。

translations.literal: and when men's talk comes, you again push it away and will not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: and when that talk arrives, you push it away and refuse to hear it.

sentences.zh: 不知平日之際遇信任者，肯為陛下分此謗乎？

translations.literal: Do you not know whether those you favor and trust in ordinary times are willing to share this slander for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Do those you favor and trust in ordinary times share this blame on your behalf?

sentences.zh: 無也。

translations.literal: They will not.
translations.idiomatic: They will not.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能布所失於天下，而不必曲為之回護，凡人言之所不貸者，一朝赫然而盡去之，務使蠹根悉拔，孽種不留，如日月之更，如風雷之迅，則天下之謗，不改而自息矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can truly publish your faults to the realm and need not bend to shield them, and all whom men's talk will not spare are in one morning brilliantly removed altogether, striving to pull out every worm-eaten root and leave no evil seed, like the change of sun and moon, like the swiftness of wind and thunder, then the realm's slander, without being altered, will cease of itself.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would openly acknowledge your faults to the realm instead of bending to shield them, and in one swift stroke remove all whom public talk condemns, uprooting every rotten root and leaving no evil seed—swift as sun and moon, sharp as wind and thunder—then slander would die away without your having to answer it.

sentences.zh: 陛下何憚何疑而不為此哉！

translations.literal: What does Your Majesty fear or doubt, that you do not do this!
translations.idiomatic: What fear or doubt keeps Your Majesty from doing this!

sentences.zh: 又極言邊事，曲盡事情。

translations.literal: He also spoke to the utmost on frontier affairs, exhaustively setting forth the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke at length on frontier affairs, laying out the situation in full detail.

sentences.zh: 以直寶謨閣知婺州。

translations.literal: He was made direct academician of the Baomo Pavilion and prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed direct academician of the Baomo Pavilion and prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書少監，拜司農卿，復為秘書少監，進太常少卿兼中書門下檢正諸房公事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, appointed Minister of Agriculture, again made Vice Director of the Secretariat, and advanced to Vice Minister of Rites while concurrently serving as rectifier of the various offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, made Minister of Agriculture, returned to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and advanced to Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent duty rectifying the various offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人，升起居郎兼權刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Diarist, then advanced to Senior Diarist while concurrently acting as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Diarist, then Senior Diarist with acting duty as Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 臣僚論罷，以集英殿修撰提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: After criticism by fellow officials he was dismissed and made Compiler at the Hall for Gathering Excellence with charge of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Criticized by fellow officials, he was dismissed and made Compiler at the Hall for Gathering Excellence with charge of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 起，再知婺州，辭免，復舊祠。

translations.literal: He was recalled, again made prefect of Wuzhou, declined and was excused, and restored to his former sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and again offered Wuzhou, but declined and was excused, returning to his former sinecure post.

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年，召至闕，授權吏部侍郎兼權中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunyou he was summoned to court and appointed acting Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent acting Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In 1244 (Chunyou 4) he was summoned to court and made acting Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent acting Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 尋為吏部侍郎仍兼權中書舍人、兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Vice Minister of Personnel while still holding concurrent acting Secretariat Drafter and Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Minister of Personnel while retaining acting Secretariat Drafter and Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 時暫兼權侍右侍郎，兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: At the time he was temporarily also acting Attendant Right Vice Minister, and concurrently Compiler of the National History and Co-compiler of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: For a time he also served as acting Attendant Right Vice Minister while compiling the National History and co-compiling the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 權刑部尚書，尋為真。

translations.literal: He was acting Minister of Punishments, and soon received the full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting Minister of Punishments and soon confirmed in the post.

sentences.zh: 七年，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs with concurrent acting Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1247 he was appointed Duanming Hall academician and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs with acting duty as Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 八年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1248 he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 以監察御史陳垓論罷，以資政殿學士知建寧府。

translations.literal: Dismissed on impeachment by Investigating Censor Chen Gai, he was made Academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: After Investigating Censor Chen Gai memorialized for his dismissal, he was made Zizheng Hall academician and prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 寶祐元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoyou he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1253 (Baoyou 1).

sentences.zh: 鄭寀，不詳何郡人。

translations.literal: Zheng Cai—it is not clear from which commandery he came.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Cai; his native commandery is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 初歷官為秘書省校書郎兼國史編修、實錄檢討。

translations.literal: His first offices were Collator of the Secretariat while also compiler of the National History and examiner of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Collator of the Secretariat, concurrently compiling the National History and examining the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 遷著作佐郎兼權侍右郎官，升著作郎兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Compiler while concurrently acting as Attendant Right Bureau Gentleman, then advanced to Compiler while also serving as Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant Compiler with acting duty as Attendant Right Bureau Gentleman, then to Compiler and Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 拜右正言，言：「丞相史嵩之以父憂去，遽欲起之，意甚厚也。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Rectifier and said: "The chief councillor Shi Songzhi left office on his father's mourning, yet you hasten to recall him—the intention is very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Right Rectifier, he said: "Chief Councillor Shi Songzhi has left office for his father's mourning, yet Your Majesty hastens to recall him—a generous intention indeed.

sentences.zh: 奈何謗議未息，事關名教，有尼其行。」

translations.literal: Yet how can it be—slander and criticism have not ceased; the matter touches the teaching of names and norms, and there is what obstructs his course."
translations.idiomatic: Yet slander has not died down; the matter touches ritual propriety, and obstacles stand in the way."

sentences.zh: 帝答曰：「卿言雖切事理，進退大臣豈易事也！」

translations.literal: The emperor replied: "Your words, though keen to the facts and principle, advancing and dismissing great ministers—is that an easy matter!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Your words hit the mark, but appointing and dismissing great ministers is no easy matter!"

sentences.zh: 擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attending Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attending Censor within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「台諫以糾察官邪為職，國之紀綱係焉。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "The censorate and remonstrance bureau take correction of official wrongdoing as their duty; the state's discipline depends on them.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "The censorate and remonstrance offices exist to correct official misconduct; the state's discipline depends on them.

sentences.zh: 比劉漢弼劾奏司農卿謝逵，陛下已行其言矣，未及兩月，忽復敘用，何其速也！

translations.literal: Recently Liu Hanbi impeached and memorialized against Minister of Agriculture Xie Kui; Your Majesty already carried out his words—yet before two months had passed, he was suddenly restored to office. How swift that was!
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hanbi impeached Minister of Agriculture Xie Kui, Your Majesty acted on his charge—yet within two months Xie was suddenly restored. How swift was that reversal!

sentences.zh: 漢弼雖亡，官不可廢。

translations.literal: Though Hanbi is dead, the office cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Hanbi is dead, but his office cannot be rendered meaningless.

sentences.zh: 臣非為漢弼惜，為朝廷惜也。」

translations.literal: Your servant does not grieve for Hanbi; he grieves for the court."
translations.idiomatic: I do not grieve for Hanbi; I grieve for the court."

sentences.zh: 又奏劾王瓚、龔基先、胡清獻，鐫秩罷祠，皆從之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized impeaching Wang Zan, Gong Jixian, and Hu Qingxian, requesting demotion of rank and dismissal from sinecure posts; all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Wang Zan, Gong Jixian, and Hu Qingxian, seeking their demotion and removal from sinecure posts; the emperor approved all three.

sentences.zh: 三人者，不才臺諫也。

translations.literal: These three were incompetent censors and remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: All three were unworthy censors and remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「比年以來，舊章寢廢。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "In recent years old regulations have lain dormant and been abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "In recent years established regulations have fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 外而諸閫，不問勳勞之有無，而爵秩皆得以例遷；

translations.literal: Externally, among the various circuits, whether merit and toil exist or not is not asked, yet ranks and titles may all advance by precedent;
translations.idiomatic: In the circuits, merit no longer matters—ranks and titles advance by routine alone;

sentences.zh: 內而侍從，不問才業之憂劣，而職位皆可以例進。

translations.literal: internally, among attendants-in-waiting, whether talent and achievement are superior or inferior is not asked, yet posts may all advance by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: within the court, talent no longer counts—attendant posts advance by routine alone.

sentences.zh: 執政之歸休田里者，與之貼職可也，而凡補外者，皆授之矣。

translations.literal: For chief councillors returning to rest in their villages, giving them nominal posts would suffice, yet all who fill outer posts are given such appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Retired chief councillors might receive nominal posts, yet every outer appointment is handed out the same way.

sentences.zh: 故自公侯以至節度，有同序補，自書殿以至秘閣，錯立周行。

translations.literal: Thus from dukes and marquises down to military commissioners there is sequential appointment alike; from the Hall of Literature down to the Secret Archive posts stand jumbled in the same ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Thus from dukes and marquises down to military commissioners, appointments follow the same sequence; from the Hall of Literature to the Secret Archive, offices crowd the same ranks.

sentences.zh: 名器之輕，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: In the cheapening of titles and regalia, nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Never has the devaluation of honors been so extreme.

sentences.zh: 無功者受賞，則何以旌有功之士；

translations.literal: When the meritless receive reward, how can meritorious men be commended?
translations.idiomatic: When the undeserving are rewarded, how can the meritorious be honored?

sentences.zh: 有罪者假寵，則何以服無罪之人。

translations.literal: When the guilty receive borrowed favor, how can the guiltless be satisfied?
translations.idiomatic: When the guilty receive favor, how can the innocent be persuaded?

sentences.zh: 矧事變無窮，而名器有限，使名器常重於上，則人心不敢輕視於下，非才而罔功者不得覬幸於其間，則負慷慨之氣、懷功名之願者，陛下始可得而鼓舞之矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, affairs change without end while titles and regalia are limited; if titles and regalia are always weighty above, then men's hearts below will not dare treat them lightly, and those without talent who claim merit falsely cannot hope for advantage among them—then men who bear generous spirit and harbor the wish for achievement and fame, Your Majesty may at last inspire and rouse them."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, crises are endless while honors are finite; if honors remain weighty at court, men below will not treat them lightly, and the talentless who claim merit cannot hope for reward—then men of generous spirit who seek achievement, Your Majesty may at last inspire them."

sentences.zh: 遷左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 淳祐七年，拜端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chunyou he was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Associate Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1247 (Chunyou 7) he was made Academician of the Duanming Hall and Associate Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以監察御史陳求魯論罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on the criticism of Investigating Censor Chen Qiulu.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed after Investigating Censor Chen Qiulu memorialized against him.

sentences.zh: 淳祐九年五月，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year of Chunyou he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of 1249 (Chunyou 9).

sentences.zh: 寀之居言路，嘗按工部侍郎曹豳、主管吏部架閣文字洪芹，則大傷公論云。

translations.literal: While Cai held the path of remonstrance he once prosecuted Vice Minister of Works Cao Bin and Hong Qin, supervisor of Ministry of Personnel archive documents—it is said this greatly wounded public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as a remonstrator, Cai once prosecuted Vice Minister of Works Cao Bin and Hong Qin, supervisor of Ministry of Personnel archive documents—a move said to have gravely offended public opinion.

sentences.zh: 應㒡，字之道，慶元府昌國人。

translations.literal: Ying You, courtesy name Zhidao, was a man of Changguo in Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ying You, styled Zhidao, was from Changguo in Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 刻志於學。

translations.literal: He carved his will into learning.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself single-mindedly to study.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十六年，試南省第一，遂舉進士，為臨江軍教授。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiading he ranked first in the southern provincial examination, then passed the jinshi and became professor of Linjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1223 (Jiading 16) he placed first in the metropolitan examination, received his jinshi degree, and was appointed professor at Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 入為國子學錄兼莊文府教授。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Recorder of the Directorate of Education while also professor of the Zhuangwen Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was called to the capital as Recorder of the Directorate of Education and professor of the Zhuangwen Palace.

sentences.zh: 遷太學博士，又遷秘書郎，請蚤建太子。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then to Secretary, and requested that the heir apparent be established early.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then Secretary, and urged the early establishment of a crown prince.

sentences.zh: 入對，帝問星變，㒡請「修實德以答天戒」。

translations.literal: Presenting himself at audience, when the emperor asked about astral anomalies, You requested to "cultivate real virtue to answer Heaven's warning."
translations.idiomatic: At audience, when the emperor asked about celestial omens, You urged him to "cultivate genuine virtue to answer Heaven's warning."

sentences.zh: 帝問州縣貪風，㒡曰：「貪黷由殉色而起。

translations.literal: The emperor asked about the wind of greed in prefectures and counties; You said: "Corruption and extortion arise from devotion to sensual pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about corruption in the prefectures and counties, You said: "Graft arises from indulgence in sensual pleasure.

sentences.zh: 成湯製官刑，儆有位，首及於巫風淫風者，有以也。」

translations.literal: King Tang instituted official punishments to warn those who hold office, putting first those of shaman wind and licentious wind—there was reason in it."
translations.idiomatic: King Tang instituted official punishments to warn those in office, targeting first those given to shamanry and licentiousness—and he had good reason."

sentences.zh: 帝問藏書，㒡請「訪先儒解經注史」，因及程迥、張根所著書皆有益世教。

translations.literal: The emperor asked about the book collection; You requested to "seek out former Confucians' commentaries on the classics and annotations on history," and mentioned that the books written by Cheng Jiong and Zhang Gen were all beneficial to worldly teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the imperial library, You urged the court to "seek out former Confucians' commentaries on the classics and histories," noting that works by Cheng Jiong and Zhang Gen were all of benefit to moral education.

sentences.zh: 帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書省著作佐郎兼權尚左郎官、兼翰林權直。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Compiler of the Secretariat while concurrently acting as Senior Left Bureau Gentleman and acting duty officer of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant Compiler of the Secretariat with acting duty as Senior Left Bureau Gentleman and acting Hanlin duty officer.

sentences.zh: 又遷著作郎，仍兼職，以言罷。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Compiler while still holding concurrent posts, and was dismissed on account of his remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Compiler while retaining his concurrent posts, but was dismissed for his outspoken remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 淳祐二年，敘復奉祠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunyou he was restored by seniority to a sinecure post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1242 (Chunyou 2) he was restored to a sinecure post by seniority.

sentences.zh: 遷宗正寺丞兼權禮部郎官，兼國史編修、實錄檢討，以言罷。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan while concurrently acting as Ministry of Rites Gentleman, and also compiler of the National History and examiner of the Veritable Records; he was dismissed on account of his remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan with acting duty in the Ministry of Rites, concurrently compiling the National History and examining the Veritable Records, but was again dismissed for remonstrating.

sentences.zh: 差知台州，召兼禮部郎官、崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: He was assigned to know Taizhou, then summoned to concurrent duty as Ministry of Rites Gentleman and Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned prefect of Taizhou, then recalled to concurrent duty as Ministry of Rites Gentleman and Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書少監，仍兼職，兼權直學士院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat while still holding concurrent posts, and given concurrent acting duty in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat while retaining his concurrent posts and given acting duty in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 又遷起居舍人、權兵部侍郎，時暫兼權吏部侍郎兼直學士院，帝一夕召㒡草麻，夜四鼓，五製皆就，帝奇其才。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Diarist and acting Vice Minister of War; at the time he was temporarily also acting Vice Minister of Personnel while serving in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies. One evening the emperor summoned You to draft edicts; by the fourth watch of the night five documents were all completed, and the emperor marveled at his talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Diarist and acting Vice Minister of War, and for a time also acting Vice Minister of Personnel with duty in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies. One night the emperor summoned him to draft edicts; by the fourth watch all five were finished, and the emperor marveled at his ability.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎仍兼職。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel while still holding concurrent posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel while retaining his concurrent posts.

sentences.zh: 進翰林學士兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Hanlin Academician while also serving as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 八年，授同知樞密院事兼參知政事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs while also Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 九年拜參知政事，封臨海郡侯，乞歸田里。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery, enfeoffed as Marquis of Linhai Commandery, and requested to return to his village.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery, enfeoffed as Marquis of Linhai, and asked to retire to his home district.

sentences.zh: 以資政殿學士知平江府，提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He was made Academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Pingjiang, with charge of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Pingjiang, with charge of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 寶祐三年，殿中侍御史丁大全論罷，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoyou, Attending Censor within the Palace Ding Daquan memorialized for his dismissal; soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1255 (Baoyou 3), Attending Censor Ding Daquan memorialized for his dismissal; he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，詔復元職致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou an edict restored his original post for retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 (Deyou 1) an edict restored his original rank in retirement.

sentences.zh: 徐清叟

translations.literal: Xu Qingsou
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qingsou

sentences.zh: 徐清叟，字直翁，煥章閣學士應龍之子。

translations.literal: Xu Qingsou, courtesy name Zhiweng, was the son of Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion Xu Yinglong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qingsou, styled Zhiweng, was the son of Xu Yinglong, Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the seventh year of Jiading (1214).

sentences.zh: 曆主管戶部架閣，遷籍田令。

translations.literal: He served in succession as supervisor of the Ministry of Revenue archives and was transferred to Registrar of Crown Lands.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as supervisor of the Ministry of Revenue archives and was promoted to Registrar of Crown Lands.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「邇者江右、閩嶠，盜賊竊發，監司帥守，未免少立威名，專行誅戮，此特以權濟事而已。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Recently in Jiangxi and the Fujian hill country bandits have broken out in secret; the circuit supervisors and military prefects cannot avoid somewhat establishing their authority and carrying out executions exclusively—this is merely using expedient authority to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Of late bandits have flared up in Jiangxi and the Fujian hill country. The circuit supervisors and military prefects, wishing to make a name for themselves, have resorted chiefly to executions—an expedient use of power, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 而偏州僻壘，習熟見聞，轉相仿效，亦皆不俟論報，輒行專殺。

translations.literal: But remote prefectures and secluded garrisons, accustomed to what they have seen and heard, one after another imitate the practice, and all likewise without awaiting review and report carry out unauthorized killings.
translations.idiomatic: Remote prefectures and isolated garrisons, having grown used to such examples, followed suit; everywhere men killed without awaiting imperial review or report.

sentences.zh: 欲望明行禁止，一變臣下嗜殺希進之心，以無墜祖宗立國仁厚之意。」

translations.literal: Your subject desires that an explicit prohibition be issued to transform once and for all the hearts of officials who love killing and hope to advance, so as not to fall short of the humane and generous intent with which the founding ancestors established the state."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to forbid this plainly and uproot the officials' craving for bloodshed as a path to promotion, lest we betray the humane magnanimity with which our founders built the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 遷軍器監主簿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk of the Directorate of Armaments.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made chief clerk of the Directorate of Armaments.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：「太后舉哀之日，陛下以後服下同媵妾，令別置大袖一襲。

translations.literal: At an audience he said: "On the day the Empress Dowager observed mourning, Your Majesty wore the empress's mourning garb in the same manner as a concubine-attendant, ordering that a separate set of wide sleeves be provided.
translations.idiomatic: At court he said: "When the Empress Dowager entered mourning, Your Majesty wore the empress's mourning dress in the same style as a lesser consort, with a separate set of wide sleeves provided.

sentences.zh: 文思院觀望，欲如後飾，再造其一以進，詔卻之。

translations.literal: The Palace Atelier watched the situation and, wishing to make it like the empress's ornaments, fabricated another set to present; an edict refused it.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Atelier, taking its cue, tried to duplicate the empress's regalia and present a second set; the emperor ordered it rejected.

sentences.zh: 此真知嫡庶之辨者。

translations.literal: This truly knows the distinction between principal wife and lesser consort.
translations.idiomatic: This showed a true grasp of the distinction between legitimate wife and concubine.

sentences.zh: 請宣付史館，以垂法後世。」

translations.literal: I request that this be proclaimed and filed in the Historiography Institute, to hand down as law for posterity."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this be recorded in the Historiography Office as a lesson for future ages."

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 入對，疏言：「陛下親政以來，精神少振而氣脈未復，條目畢舉而綱紀未張，公道若伸而私意之未盡克者，則亦風化之先務，勸戒之大權，與夫選用之要術，猶有闕略而未之講明者爾。

translations.literal: At an audience he submitted a memorial saying: "Since Your Majesty began personal rule, your spirit has revived somewhat but the vital pulse has not yet recovered; items have all been raised but the framework has not yet been spread; public justice seems extended but private wishes not yet fully overcome—then also the foremost tasks of transforming customs, the great authority of admonition and restraint, and the essential techniques of selection and employment still have gaps and omissions that have not been explained and clarified.
translations.idiomatic: At an audience he submitted a lengthy memorial: "Since Your Majesty took personal rule in hand, your energy has stirred somewhat but the dynasty's pulse has not fully returned; programs are launched but discipline is not yet restored; public justice advances yet private interest is not wholly subdued. The foremost tasks of moral reform, the great leverage of admonition and restraint, and the essential art of appointing talent—all still lack clear exposition.

sentences.zh: 何謂風化之先務？

translations.literal: What is meant by the foremost tasks of transforming customs?
translations.idiomatic: What are the foremost tasks of moral reform?

sentences.zh: 曰原人倫以釋群惑者是已。

translations.literal: It is said: to trace human relations to dispel the confusion of the multitude—that is it.
translations.idiomatic: It is to return to the foundations of human relations and dispel public confusion.

sentences.zh: 何謂勸戒之大權？

translations.literal: What is meant by the great authority of admonition and restraint?
translations.idiomatic: What is the great leverage of admonition and restraint?

sentences.zh: 曰惜名器以示正義者是已。

translations.literal: It is said: to cherish titles and insignia to display rectitude and justice—that is it.
translations.idiomatic: It is to treasure offices and honors so as to uphold right and justice.

sentences.zh: 何謂選用之要術？

translations.literal: What is meant by the essential techniques of selection and employment?
translations.idiomatic: What are the essential techniques of selection and appointment?

sentences.zh: 曰因物望而進人才者是已。」

translations.literal: It is said: to rely on public repute and advance men of talent—that is it."
translations.idiomatic: It is to advance talent according to genuine public esteem."

sentences.zh: 蓋欲請復皇子竑王爵，裁抑史彌遠恤典，召用真德秀、魏了翁也。

translations.literal: — in substance wishing to request restoration of Prince Gou's princely title, curtailment of Shi Miyuan's mourning honors, and summons to employ Zhen Dexiu and Wei Liaoweng.
translations.idiomatic: — in substance he was urging restoration of Prince Gou's princely rank, reduction of Shi Miyuan's posthumous honors, and recall of Zhen Dexiu and Wei Liaoweng.

sentences.zh: 兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: He also served concurrently as lecturer of the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as lecturer of the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書郎，升著作佐郎兼權司封郎官，遷軍器少監，皆兼職依舊。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretary; promoted to Associate Compiler with acting concurrent Bureau Gentleman of the Directorate of Honors; transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Armaments—all concurrent posts remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Secretary, then promoted to Associate Compiler with acting charge of the Directorate of Honors, then Vice Director of Armaments, retaining all his concurrent posts.

sentences.zh: 遷將作監，拜殿中侍御史兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of Palace Construction and appointed Palace Censor with concurrent lectureship.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of Palace Construction and Palace Censor with concurrent lectureship.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿兼權戶部侍郎兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with acting concurrent Vice Minister of Revenue and lectureship.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Rites with acting charge of the Ministry of Revenue and a concurrent lectureship.

sentences.zh: 三疏丐外，給事中洪谘夔、起居舍人吳泳皆抗疏留之。

translations.literal: Three times he memorialized begging for an outer post; Attendant Gentleman Hong Ziqi and Diary Attendant Wu Yong all submitted blocking memorials to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he asked to leave the capital; Attendant Gentleman Hong Ziqi and Diary Attendant Wu Yong each submitted memorials urging that he be kept at court.

sentences.zh: 尋權工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he held acting appointment as Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given acting appointment as Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 以右文殿修撰知泉州，集英殿修撰知靜江府、廣西經略安撫使。

translations.literal: As Compiler of the Youwen Hall he was prefect of Quanzhou; as Compiler of the Jiying Hall he was prefect of Jingjiang and Guangxi Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As Compiler of the Youwen Hall he governed Quanzhou; as Compiler of the Jiying Hall he governed Jingjiang as Guangxi Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遷侍右侍郎、主管雲臺觀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Gentleman of the Right and placed in charge of the Yuntai Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Senior Gentleman of the Right and placed in charge of the Yuntai Observatory.

sentences.zh: 召赴闕，遷戶部侍郎，再為侍右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned to court, transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, and again made Senior Gentleman of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he was made Vice Minister of Revenue and again appointed Senior Gentleman of the Right.

sentences.zh: 以寶章閣直學士知溫州，改知福建安撫使，改知婺州。

translations.literal: As Direct Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion he was prefect of Wenzhou; he was changed to Fujian Pacification Commissioner and then to prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Direct Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion he governed Wenzhou, then served as Fujian Pacification Commissioner, then as prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 以煥章閣直學士差知泉州，辭免。

translations.literal: As Direct Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion he was assigned to govern Quanzhou and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned to govern Quanzhou as Direct Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion, he declined the post.

sentences.zh: 改知袁州，又改知紹興府、兩浙東路安撫使，辭免。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Yuanzhou, then again to Shaoxing and Eastern Zhejiang Pacification Commissioner, and declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Yuanzhou, then to Shaoxing as Eastern Zhejiang Pacification Commissioner, and declined both appointments.

sentences.zh: 改知潭州，尋知廣州兼廣東經略安撫使。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Tanzhou; soon after he was prefect of Guangzhou with concurrent Guangdong Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Tanzhou and soon after governed Guangzhou as Guangdong Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召赴闕，權兵部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was summoned to court and given acting appointment as Minister of War with concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he was given acting appointment as Minister of War with concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 淳祐九年，兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰，權吏部尚書，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Chunyou he served concurrently as Compiler of the National History and Co-compiler of the Veritable Records, as acting Minister of Personnel, and was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1249 (Chunyou 9) he was made concurrent Compiler of the National History and Co-compiler of the Veritable Records, acting Minister of Personnel, and then Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事，進同知樞密院事，封晉寧郡公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, advanced to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinning.

sentences.zh: 奏修《四朝國史》志傳，五上章乞改機政，帝不許。

translations.literal: He memorialized to compile the annals and biographies of the Four Dynasties National History; five times he submitted memorials begging to leave central government affairs; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed compiling the annals and biographies for the Four Dynasties National History and five times asked to leave the central government; the emperor refused each time.

sentences.zh: 十二年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1252 he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 尋知樞密院事兼參知政事，監察御史朱應元論罷，以資政殿大學士提舉玉隆萬壽宮，改洞霄宮，復以監察御史朱熠論罷。

translations.literal: Soon he was Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs with concurrent Vice Grand Councillor; Investigating Censor Zhu Yingyuan impeached him and he was dismissed, made Grand Academician of the Zizheng Hall administering the Yulong Longevity Palace, changed to the Dongxiao Palace, and again dismissed on impeachment by Investigating Censor Zhu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs while retaining his vice-councillor post, but Investigating Censor Zhu Yingyuan impeached him and he was dismissed to administer the Yulong Longevity Palace as Grand Academician of the Zizheng Hall; transferred to the Dongxiao Palace, he was dismissed again on impeachment by Investigating Censor Zhu Yi.

sentences.zh: 久之，以舊職提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: After a long time, with his former post he administered the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he returned to his former duty administering the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 開慶元年，召赴闕，以舊職提舉佑神觀兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiqing he was summoned to court and, with his former post, administered the Youshen Observatory with concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In 1259 (Kaiqing 1) he was summoned to court to administer the Youshen Observatory with concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 出知泉州，復提舉佑神觀。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Quanzhou and again administered the Youshen Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to govern Quanzhou, then again took charge of the Youshen Observatory.

sentences.zh: 景定三年，轉兩官致仕，卒，贈少師，諡忠簡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingding he was advanced two ranks and retired; he died; posthumously made Junior Mentor; posthumous title Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1262 (Jingding 3) he was advanced two ranks and retired; he died and was posthumously made Junior Mentor with the posthumous title Zhongjian (Loyal and Plain).

sentences.zh: 清叟父子兄弟皆以風節相尚，而清叟劾罷袁甫，於公論少貶云。

translations.literal: Qingsou's father, sons, and brothers all prized one another for integrity of character, yet Qingsou impeached Yuan Fu to dismissal, and in public opinion he was somewhat diminished, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The Qingsou family—father, sons, and brothers—were all known for their integrity, yet because Qingsou impeached Yuan Fu out of office, public esteem for him was somewhat diminished.

sentences.zh: 李曾伯

translations.literal: Li Cengbo
translations.idiomatic: Li Cengbo

sentences.zh: 李曾伯，字長孺，覃懷人，後居嘉興。

translations.literal: Li Cengbo, courtesy name Changru, was a man of Tanhuai and later resided in Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cengbo, styled Changru, was a native of Tanhuai who later settled in Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 歷官通判濠州，遷軍器監主簿，添差通判鄂州兼沿江制置副使司主管機宜文字。

translations.literal: In succession he served as vice-prefect of Bozhou, was transferred to chief clerk of the Directorate of Armaments, and was given additional assignment as vice-prefect of Ezhou with concurrent staff officer for military affairs of the Riverine Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as vice-prefect of Bozhou and chief clerk of the Directorate of Armaments, then held additional appointment as vice-prefect of Ezhou with concurrent staff officer for the Riverine Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 遷度支郎官，授左司郎官、淮西總領。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bureau Gentleman of the Revenue Section and appointed Left Bureau Gentleman and Huai West Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Bureau Gentleman of the Revenue Section, then appointed Left Bureau Gentleman and Huai West Intendant.

sentences.zh: 尋遷右司郎官，太府少卿兼左司郎官，兼敕令所刪修官。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Bureau Gentleman, Vice Director of the Palace Stores with concurrent Left Bureau Gentleman, and concurrent reviser at the Statute Revision Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Right Bureau Gentleman and Vice Director of the Palace Stores while retaining his Left Bureau post, and served concurrently as reviser at the Statute Revision Office.

sentences.zh: 遷太府卿、淮東制置使兼淮西制置使，詔軍事便宜行之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Stores, Huai East Pacification Commissioner with concurrent Huai West Pacification Commissioner; an edict ordered that military affairs be carried out at his convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Palace Stores and Pacification Commissioner for both Huai East and Huai West, with authority to handle military affairs as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 曾伯疏奏三事：答天心，重地勢，協人謀。

translations.literal: Cengbo memorialized three matters: respond to Heaven's mind, weight terrain, and harmonize human counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Cengbo memorialized on three points: heed Heaven's will, secure the terrain, and align human strategy.

sentences.zh: 又言：「邊餉貴於廣積，將材貴於素儲，賞與不可以不精，戰士不可以不恤。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Frontier provisions value broad accumulation; general talent values long-standing storage; rewards and grants must not be careless; fighting troops must not go uncherished."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Frontier supplies depend on ample stockpiles; commanders must be cultivated well in advance; rewards must be dispensed with care; and the fighting men must not be neglected."

sentences.zh: 又條上：「淮麵舟師之所當戒，湖麵險阻之所當治。」

translations.literal: He also listed in detail: "The Huai front is where naval forces must be on guard; the lake front is rugged terrain that must be managed."
translations.idiomatic: He further set forth: "The Huai frontier demands vigilance from the river fleets; the lake frontier's difficult terrain must be brought under control."

sentences.zh: 加華文閣待制，又加寶章閣直學士，進權兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Prepared Scholar of the Huawen Pavilion, then to Direct Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, and advanced to acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Prepared Scholar of the Huawen Pavilion, then Direct Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion, and advanced to acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 淳祐六年正月朔，日食。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chunyou, on the new moon of the first month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of 1246 (Chunyou 6), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 曾伯應詔，歷陳先朝因天象以謹邊備、圖帥材，乞早易閫寄，放歸田里。

translations.literal: Cengbo responded to the imperial decree, reviewing in detail how the former court used celestial signs to tighten frontier defenses and plan commanders' talent, and begged that border command be changed early and that he be released to return to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: Responding to the imperial summons, Cengbo reviewed how earlier reigns had used celestial warnings to tighten frontier defenses and cultivate commanders, and asked to be relieved of border command and sent home to his estate.

sentences.zh: 又請修浚泗州西城。

translations.literal: He also requested dredging and repair of the western city of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested dredging and repair of the western quarter of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 加煥章閣學士，言者相繼論罷。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion; critics in succession impeached him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion, but successive impeachments by critics led to his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 九年，以舊職知靜江府、廣西經略安撫使，兼廣西轉運使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, with his former post he was prefect of Jingjiang and Guangxi Pacification Commissioner, with concurrent Guangxi Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1249 he returned to his former duties as prefect of Jingjiang and Guangxi Pacification Commissioner, with concurrent charge of Guangxi transport.

sentences.zh: 陳守邊之宜五事。

translations.literal: He presented five points on what is fitting in guarding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He presented five recommendations on frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 進徽猷閣學士、京湖安撫制置使、知江陵府，兼湖廣總領，兼京湖屯田使，進龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Academician of the Huixuan Pavilion, Jing-Hu Pacification Commissioner, prefect of Jiangling, with concurrent Huguang Intendant and Jing-Hu Colonization Commissioner, and advanced to Academician of the Longtu Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician of the Huixuan Pavilion, Jing-Hu Pacification Commissioner, and prefect of Jiangling, with concurrent charge of Huguang supplies and Jing-Hu colonization, and then to Academician of the Longtu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「襄陽新復之地，城池雖修浚，田野未加辟；

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Xiangyang is newly recovered territory; though the city walls have been dredged and repaired, the fields have not yet been opened;
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Xiangyang is newly recovered territory. Though the walls have been repaired, the fields remain uncultivated;

sentences.zh: 室廬雖草創，市井未阜通。

translations.literal: though houses have been roughly built, the markets are not yet flourishing and connected.
translations.idiomatic: though shelters have been hastily erected, commerce has not yet revived.

sentences.zh: 請蠲租三年。」

translations.literal: I request rent remission for three years."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that land tax be remitted for three years."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 加端明殿學士兼夔路策應大使。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Academician of the Duanming Hall with concurrent Kuizhou Response Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Duanming Hall with concurrent appointment as Kuizhou Response Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 進資政殿學士，制置四川邊麵，與執政恩例。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Academician of the Zizheng Hall, commissioner for the Sichuan frontier, with the same favors as chief councillors.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Academician of the Zizheng Hall and made commissioner for the Sichuan frontier with privileges equal to those of the chief councillors.

sentences.zh: 尋授四川宣撫使，特賜同進士出身。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Sichuan Pacification Commissioner and specially granted jinshi equivalency.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Sichuan Pacification Commissioner and specially granted jinshi status.

sentences.zh: 召赴闕，加大學士，知福州兼福建安撫使。

translations.literal: He was summoned to court, given the additional title Grand Academician, and made prefect of Fuzhou with concurrent Fujian Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he was made Grand Academician and appointed prefect of Fuzhou with concurrent charge as Fujian Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 辭免，以大學士提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He declined; as Grand Academician he administered the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the appointment and retired to administer the Dongxiao Palace as Grand Academician.

sentences.zh: 起為湖南安撫大使兼知潭州，兼節制廣南，移治靜江。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Hunan Pacification Grand Commissioner with concurrent prefect of Tanzhou and control over Guangnan, and transferred his administration to Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was made Hunan Pacification Grand Commissioner and prefect of Tanzhou with authority over Guangnan, and moved his headquarters to Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 開慶元年，進觀文殿學士，以諫議大夫沈炎等論罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiqing he was advanced to Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and was dismissed on criticism by Remonstrance Grandee Shen Yan and others.
translations.idiomatic: In 1259 (Kaiqing 1) he was promoted to Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature but was dismissed after Remonstrance Grandee Shen Yan and others memorialized against him.

sentences.zh: 景定五年，起知慶元府兼沿海制置使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingding he was recalled to govern Qingyuan Prefecture with concurrent Coastal Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1264 (Jingding 5) he was recalled to govern Qingyuan as Coastal Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸淳元年，殿中侍御史陳宗禮論劾，褫職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianchun, Attending Censor within the Palace Chen Zongli impeached him and his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In 1265 (Xianchun 1), Attending Censor Chen Zongli impeached him and he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，追復元官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou his original rank was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 (Deyou 1) an edict restored his original rank.

sentences.zh: 曾伯初與賈似道俱為閫帥，邊境之事，知無不言。

translations.literal: Cengbo at first, together with Jia Sidao, were both frontier commanders; on border affairs, whatever he knew he spoke without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Cengbo had early served alongside Jia Sidao as a frontier commander and spoke frankly on every matter he knew concerning the border.

sentences.zh: 似道卒嫉之，使不竟其用云。

translations.literal: Sidao in the end grew jealous of him, causing his talents not to be fully employed, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao ultimately came to resent him, and his talents were never fully put to use.

sentences.zh: 王野，字子文，寶章閣待制介之子也。

translations.literal: Wang Ye, courtesy name Ziwen, was the son of Prepared Scholar Jie of the Baozhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ye, styled Ziwen, was the son of Jie, Prepared Scholar of the Baozhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 以父陰補官，登嘉定十二年進士第。

translations.literal: By his father's yin privilege he received office; he passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through his father's yin privilege and received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of Jiading (1219).

sentences.zh: 仕潭時，帥真德秀一見異之，延致幕下，遂執弟子禮。

translations.literal: When he served in Tan, the commander Zhen Dexiu at first sight marked him as unusual, invited him to his staff, and Ye thereupon performed the rites of a disciple.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in Tanzhou, the prefect Zhen Dexiu was struck by him at first meeting, brought him onto his staff, and Ye thereafter treated him as his teacher.

sentences.zh: 德秀欲授以詞學，野曰：「所以求學者，義理之奧也。

translations.literal: Dexiu wished to teach him the belles-lettres examination curriculum; Ye said: "What I seek in study is the profundity of moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu wished to train him for the belles-lettres examination; Ye said: "What I seek in learning is the depth of moral principle.

sentences.zh: 詞科惟強記者能之。」

translations.literal: The belles-lettres examination only those strong in memorization can manage."
translations.idiomatic: The belles-lettres examination is only for those with exceptional memories."

sentences.zh: 德秀益器重之。

translations.literal: Dexiu all the more valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Dexiu esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 紹定初，汀、邵盜作，辟議幕參讚，攝邵武縣，後復攝軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoding, bandits arose in Ting and Shao; he was recruited to the advisory staff as participating administrator, acted as magistrate of Shaowu County, and later again acted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoding era, when banditry broke out in Tingzhou and Shaowu, he was recruited to the advisory staff, served as acting magistrate of Shaowu County, and later again held acting military command.

sentences.zh: 盜起唐石，親勒兵討之。

translations.literal: When bandits rose at Tangshi, he personally led troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose at Tangshi, he personally led troops against them.

sentences.zh: 後為樞密院編修兼檢討。

translations.literal: Later he was compiler and reviser at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as compiler and reviser at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 襄、蜀事急，議遣使講和，時相依違不決。

translations.literal: Affairs in Xiang and Shu grew urgent; the court discussed sending envoys to negotiate peace, while the chief councillors vacillated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: As crises mounted in Xiangyang and Sichuan, the court debated sending peace envoys, but the chief councillors wavered and could not settle on a course.

sentences.zh: 史嵩之帥武昌，首進和議。

translations.literal: Shi Songzhi commanded at Wuchang and was the first to advance a peace proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Songzhi, commanding at Wuchang, was the first to propose making peace.

sentences.zh: 野言：「今日之事宜先定規模，並力攻守。」

translations.literal: Ye said: "Today's affairs should first fix the overall plan and unite strength in attack and defense."
translations.idiomatic: Ye said: "Today's crisis demands that we first set a clear strategy and concentrate our forces for a united offensive and defense."

sentences.zh: 上疏言八事。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth eight points.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial outlining eight measures.

sentences.zh: 繼為副都承旨，奏請「出師，絕和使，命淮東、西夾攻。

translations.literal: He was subsequently made Deputy Capital Commissioner and memorialized: "Dispatch the army, cut off peace envoys, and order Huai East and Huai West to attack in concert.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Deputy Capital Commissioner and memorialized: "Send out the armies, sever all peace negotiations, and order coordinated attacks from Huai East and Huai West.

sentences.zh: 不然，利害將深。」

translations.literal: Otherwise advantage and harm will deepen."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the damage will only grow worse."

sentences.zh: 理宗深然之，令樞密院下三閫諭旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong deeply approved; he ordered the Bureau of Military Affairs to relay instructions to the three frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong strongly agreed and ordered the Bureau of Military Affairs to convey his instructions to the three frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙元年，輪對，采事係安危者四端，而專以司馬光仁、明、武推說。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaxi, at a rotating audience, he gathered four points bearing on security and danger, and specially expounded Sima Guang's Ren, Ming, and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1237 (Jiaxi 1), at a rotating audience, he gathered four points bearing on the realm's security and expounded especially on Sima Guang's virtues of benevolence, discernment, and martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 復推廣前所言八事，以孝宗講軍實激發帝意。

translations.literal: Again he extended the eight matters spoken of before, using Emperor Xiaozong's emphasis on military substance to stir the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: He again developed his earlier eight-point program, drawing on Emperor Xiaozong's emphasis on military readiness to stir the emperor's resolve.

sentences.zh: 淳祐初，自江西赴闕，奏祈天永命十事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunyou, coming from Jiangxi to court, he memorialized the Ten Matters of Praying Heaven for an Enduring Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunyou era he came from Jiangxi to court and presented his Ten Matters for Praying Heaven to Secure the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 嵩之起復，傾國爭之，野上疏乞聽終喪，後又言嵩之當顯絕而終斥，益嚴君子小人之限。

translations.literal: When Songzhi was recalled from mourning service, the whole realm disputed it; Ye submitted a memorial begging that he be allowed to complete his mourning; later he also said Songzhi should be clearly cut off and finally expelled, further tightening the boundary between gentlemen and petty men.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Songzhi was recalled from mourning before his term had ended, the whole court was in uproar; Ye memorialized asking that Songzhi be required to finish his mourning, and later argued that he should be definitively severed from office and finally expelled, sharpening the line between worthy ministers and unworthy ones.

sentences.zh: 拜禮部尚書，奏十事，終之曰：「陛下一心，十事之綱領也。」

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Rites, memorialized ten matters, and concluded: "Your Majesty's single-mindedness is the backbone of the ten matters."
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Minister of Rites, he memorialized ten matters and concluded: "Your Majesty's single-minded resolve is the backbone of all ten matters."

sentences.zh: 前後奏陳，皆明正剴切，鑿鑿可行。

translations.literal: Memorials before and after were all clear, upright, forceful, and solidly practicable.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials, before and after, were all lucid, forthright, and eminently practicable.

sentences.zh: 其為兩浙轉運判官，以察訪使出視江防，首嘉興至京口增修官民兵船守險備具。

translations.literal: When he was Transport Judge of the Two Zhes, as inspection envoy he went out to view river defenses; from Jiaxing to Jingkou he increased repair of official and militia ships, guarding strategic points and preparing equipment.
translations.idiomatic: As Transport Judge of the Two Zhes, he toured the river defenses as an inspection envoy and from Jiaxing to Jingkou strengthened official and militia vessels and defensive installations along the strategic points.

sentences.zh: 為江西轉運副使、知隆興府，繼有它命，時以米綱不便，就湖口造轉般倉，請事畢受代。

translations.literal: As Jiangxi Transport Vice Commissioner and prefect of Longxing, he soon received another appointment; at the time because the rice transport convoy system was inconvenient, he built a transfer granary at Hukou and requested that once the work was finished he accept replacement.
translations.idiomatic: As Jiangxi Transport Vice Commissioner and prefect of Longxing, he was soon given another appointment; finding the rice transport system cumbersome, he built a transfer granary at Hukou and asked to be relieved once the project was complete.

sentences.zh: 知鎮江府，兼都大提舉浙西兵船。

translations.literal: He was prefect of Zhenjiang with concurrent Grand Intendant of Zhe West military ships.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Zhenjiang as Grand Intendant of Zhe West military ships.

sentences.zh: 江面幾千里，調兵捍禦，以守江尤重於淮，瓜洲一渡甚狹，請免鎮江水軍調發，專一守江，置遊兵如呂蒙所言「蔣欽將萬人巡江上」，增創水艦，就揚子江習水戰，登金山指麾之。

translations.literal: The river surface extends several thousand li; deploying troops to defend it—guarding the Yangtze is especially weightier than guarding the Huai; the Guazhou crossing is very narrow. He requested exemption of Zhenjiang naval forces from outward dispatch, devoting them solely to guarding the river; he established roving troops as Lü Meng said, "Jiang Qin will lead ten thousand men to patrol the river," increased and created warships, practiced river warfare on the Yangtze, and commanded from atop Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze stretches thousands of li, and its defense matters even more than the Huai line. The crossing at Guazhou is perilously narrow. He asked that Zhenjiang's naval forces be exempted from outside deployments so they could focus solely on river defense; he established mobile patrol units, as Lü Meng had put it, "with Jiang Qin leading ten thousand men to patrol the river"; built new warships; drilled his forces in river combat on the Yangtze; and directed exercises from atop Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 是冬，揚子橋有警，急調湯孝信所領遊兵救之而退。

translations.literal: That winter there was an alarm at Yangzi Bridge; he urgently deployed the roving troops under Tang Xiaoxin's command to rescue the situation, and the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when an alarm arose at Yangzi Bridge, he urgently dispatched the mobile forces under Tang Xiaoxin; the enemy withdrew after the relief arrived.

sentences.zh: 淳祐末，遷沿江制置使、江東安撫使、節制和州無為軍安慶府兼三郡屯田、行宮留守。

translations.literal: Late in Chunyou he was transferred to Riverine Pacification Commissioner, Jiangdong Pacification Commissioner, with control over Hezhou, Wuwei Army, and Anqing Prefecture, with concurrent colonization commissioner for three prefectures and Palace Retainer.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Chunyou era he was made Riverine Pacification Commissioner and Jiangdong Pacification Commissioner, with authority over Hezhou, the Wuwei garrison, and Anqing, concurrent colonization commissioner for three prefectures, and Palace Retainer.

sentences.zh: 巡江，引水軍大閱，舳艫相銜幾三十里。

translations.literal: He patrolled the river, led the navy in a grand review, and the ships linked bow to stern for nearly thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Patrolling the river, he held a grand naval review; the vessels stretched bow to stern for nearly thirty li.

sentences.zh: 憑高望遠，考求山川險厄，謂要務莫如屯田。

translations.literal: From the heights he gazed into the distance and investigated mountains and rivers for their perilous passes, holding that in vital affairs nothing surpassed tuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed the land from high vantage points, studied the difficult terrain of mountains and rivers, and maintained that among urgent priorities nothing mattered more than frontier garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 講行事宜，修飭行宮諸殿室，推京口法，創遊擊軍萬二千，蒙衝萬艘，江上晏然。

translations.literal: He discussed and implemented affairs, repaired and put in order the various palace halls of the traveling palace, extended the Jingkou methods, created a raiding army of twelve thousand and ten thousand covered assault ships; on the Yangtze all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He deliberated military measures, refurbished the halls of the imperial traveling residence, applied the defensive model used at Jingkou, raised a twelve-thousand-man strike force and ten thousand assault vessels, and brought calm to the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 寶祐二年，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事，封吳郡侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoyou he was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 1254 he was made Duanming Hall academician and associate commissioner of military affairs, and created marquis of Wu.

sentences.zh: 與宰相不合，言者攻之，以前職主管洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He fell out with the chief counselor; critics impeached him, and he was assigned to his former duties as superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At odds with the chief minister, he came under attack from censors and was sent back to his old post as superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈七官，位特進。

translations.literal: He died; seven offices were posthumously conferred upon him, and his rank was raised to Extraordinary Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He died; the court granted seven additional posthumous offices and promoted his rank to Exalted Grandee.

sentences.zh: 野因德秀知朱熹之學，凡熹門人高弟，必加敬禮。

translations.literal: Ye through Dexiu came to know Zhu Xi's learning; all of Xi's distinguished disciples he always treated with added respect.
translations.idiomatic: Through Zhen Dexiu, Wang Ye came to know Zhu Xi's teachings, and he invariably showed distinguished disciples in Xi's school added deference.

sentences.zh: 知建寧府，創建安書院，祠熹，以德秀配。

translations.literal: As prefect of Jianning Prefecture he founded the Jian'an Academy, set up a shrine to Xi, and paired Dexiu with him in worship.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Jianning he founded Jian'an Academy, enshrined Zhu Xi there, and honored Zhen Dexiu as his associate in the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 有奏議、文集若干卷。

translations.literal: He left several scrolls of memorials and collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: His extant writings include several volumes of memorials and collected works.

sentences.zh: 野工於詩，書法祖唐歐陽詢，署書尤清勁。

translations.literal: Ye was skilled in poetry; in calligraphy he took Tang's Ouyang Xun as his ancestor, and his signature script was especially clear and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ye excelled at poetry; in calligraphy he modeled himself on the Tang master Ouyang Xun, and his signatures were especially clear and vigorous.

sentences.zh: 蔡抗，子仲節，處士元定之孫。

translations.literal: Cai Kang, courtesy name Zhongjie, was the grandson of the reclusive gentleman Yuan Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Kang, whose courtesy name was Zhongjie, was grandson of the recluse Cai Yuanding.

sentences.zh: 紹定二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoding he attained the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1229.

sentences.zh: 其後差主管尚書刑、工部架閣文字。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was assigned to supervise the archival documents of the Ministry of Punishments and Ministry of Works in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed to oversee archival records in the Secretariat's ministries of punishment and works.

sentences.zh: 召試館職，遷秘書省正字。

translations.literal: Summoned for examination for a position in the Academies, he was transferred to Rectifier in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to an academy examination, he was made a rectifier in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 升校書郎兼樞密院編修官，遷諸王宮大小學教授。
